newsitem.title: USA: TCI holds special board meeting.
newsitem.headline: TCI holds special board meeting.

text.p: The board of directors of Tele-Communications Inc., the giant cable television operator, held a special meeting on Friday amid speculation John Malone might be prepared to give up the title of president.
Malone may be keen to give up one of his titles. He is currently chairman, chief executive officer and president.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Friday that Malone may want to bring on board cable executive Leo Hindery, who currently heads up San Francisco based InterMedia Partners.
A spokesman for TCI declined to comment on the report or disclose the agenda items the board was to take up at its special meeting.
But he did say that an announcement was expected on Friday.
TCI has been having difficult days. It lost customers last year when it hiked rates and it faces serious competition from the direct broadcast satellite business.
Some observers also criticised Malone's absences from the business and have been concerned that the stock price was lingering at low levels.
Last fall Malone appeared at an industry conference, indicating he was back at the helm full time.
But worries continued and Malone had to take dramatic action.

In December TCI announced a cost-cutting programme that included layoffs of 2,500 employees, or about 6.5 percent of its workforce, salary cuts and freezes for executives. It said it would even sell its corporate planes.
On Friday TCI shares were up 25 cents at $14 on Nasdaq, up from the year low of $11.31.
TCI faces growing costs from the channels it puts on its system and has tried to scale back expenses by dropping certain channels.
But that backfired in part last month when TCI pulled Viacom Inc.'s VH1 music video channel.

It received hundreds of phone calls from irate VH1 fans and changed its plans the day before four rock stars were set to hold a press conference in Denver -- close enough to TCI's headquarters in Englewood, Colo., to prove an embarassment.
TCI executives have said the cost of programming is the fast growing one it faces and that it must choose channels carefully to satisfy viewers given that channel space is presently full.
The company recently spun off its satellite business, TCI Satellite Entertainment Inc., in hopes of creating value for its shareholders.
